instantiation.worst_case: hello.v1.HelloService/Hello now returns InvalidArgument (gRPC code 3) for any request whose name is empty or whitespace-only, where it previously returned OK with the message "hello ". If a deployed caller ever sends such a request, that call path breaks — the caller sees a non-retryable error instead of a 200. Blast radius is bounded: the fleet has exactly one cluster, e1-dev (fleet: {"id":"e1-dev","env":"dev"}); there is no staging and no prod cluster (recorded answer staging_exists="no"; deploy/envs/prod exists but no prod cluster is in the fleet); hello is ClusterIP only with no external exposure (measure exposure: two ClusterIP services, hello and hello-canary); the only measured caller is source_workload=traffic under spiffe://cluster.local/ns/frontend/sa/frontend at 2.19 rps over 1h, 3.22 rps at response_code=200, with one ready pod and an HPA ceiling of 2. Second, smaller worst case: the change breaks CI's own gates (make test / e2e/run.sh), so it never ships at all. Third: a real rise in InvalidArgument is invisible to the canary analysis, which counts only Unknown|Internal|DataLoss|DeadlineExceeded (deploy/base/rollout.yaml AnalysisTemplate server-errors), and to alerting, which does not exist (discover.yaml stack.metrics: "no alerting rules"; ALERTS query returned no data).

obligations.establish: No contract or referenced document promises that an empty name is valid input. proto/hello/v1/hello.proto declares `string name = 1;` with no validation and the service comment says Hello 'answers "hello <name>"' — proto3 cannot distinguish unset from empty, so an all-default HelloRequest was previously a legal, successful call. Establish whether the proto, README.md (the only entry under docs:) or service.yaml states anything about empty names; and confirm the author's description matches the diff — the description says 'trim the name and refuse an empty one', and the diff also silently changes the success path for non-empty padded names ('  Ada ' now yields 'hello Ada' rather than 'hello   Ada '), which is a second behaviour change the description compresses into the word 'trim'.
obligations.evidence: proto/hello/v1/hello.proto (service and message definitions); README.md; internal/handlers/hello_service.go lines 25-31 (the TrimSpace + InvalidArgument branch and greeting()); the PR description text

obligations.establish: No deployed caller sends an empty or whitespace-only name. The only authorized caller is smallStepGiantLeap/frontend (service.yaml authorizedCallers: hello.v1.HelloService/Hello; measured source_principal spiffe://cluster.local/ns/frontend/sa/frontend). Read the frontend repository's call site for hellov1.NewHelloServiceClient(...).Hello and determine whether any path can pass an unset, empty or whitespace-only Name — e.g. a pass-through of an absent HTTP query parameter or a default-constructed HelloRequest. The recorded answer traffic_generator_sends_blank_names="no" from @subganapathy (commit adf776c79637) covers only the dev load generator named 'traffic'; it is not evidence about the frontend service's own code. If such a path exists, that frontend request path now fails with InvalidArgument in e1-dev.

obligations.establish: The change is behaviour-only behind an unchanged wire contract and leaves nothing behind on rollback: the diff touches no .proto, no persisted data, no message field, no configuration schema. Confirm the proto and generated stubs in client/gen are untouched by this PR, so old and new pods accept and emit the same wire messages; rolling back to the previous image restores 'hello ' for blank names with no migration. State explicitly the mixed-version window the canary creates: during the 10% and 50% steps (deploy/base/rollout.yaml strategy.canary.steps) a blank-name caller would see InvalidArgument on some calls and OK on others — inconsistent but self-healing in either rollout direction.

obligations.establish: The change adds no load to any dependency: hello makes no outbound calls (internal/handlers/hello_service.go has no client), and the new branch returns earlier than the old success path, so CPU and in-flight time per blank request fall rather than rise. Confirm no retry amplification can turn one rejected request into many: deploy/base/mesh/virtual-service.yaml retries on the 'idempotent' route are retryOn: connect-failure,refused-stream,unavailable — InvalidArgument is not in that list — and client/client.go's ServiceConfig sets only a 10s timeout with no retryPolicy.

obligations.establish: The new path cannot sustain a failure: it adds no call, no deadline to propagate and no unbounded work (strings.TrimSpace over one field), and it fails fast with a terminal, non-retryable code. Confirm that neither the mesh (virtual-service.yaml retryOn list) nor the platform client (client/client.go, 'No retry policy here') retries InvalidArgument, so a caller that starts sending blank names produces exactly one request per request and cannot multiply load into the single hello replica.
obligations.evidence: deploy/base/mesh/virtual-service.yaml (both routes' retries blocks); client/client.go DialOptions/ServiceConfig; internal/handlers/hello_service.go:25-31

obligations.establish: Establish that the platform's own e2e still passes with this change, since its probe sends an all-default (empty) HelloRequest — e2e/probe/main.go invokes with &emptypb.Empty{}, i.e. name="". Two specific gates: (1) e2e/run.sh:339 `check reach "frontend is authorized..."` uses matches() at line 227, which accepts any output starting with CODE that is not PermissionDenied|Unavailable|DeadlineExceeded — so "CODE InvalidArgument" should still PASS; (2) the node-drain check `drain_under_load` counts a call as failed only for the probe's `failure` set (Unavailable, DeadlineExceeded, Internal, Unknown, Canceled), which excludes InvalidArgument. Verify both readings by running or reading the code; if either treats InvalidArgument as a failure, CI's e2e job fails and the change cannot ship. Note as a finding either way that after this change the in-cluster e2e no longer exercises a successful Hello response at all.

admission.is: PSS restricted, no general policy engine

autoscaler.is: KEDA scaling on in-flight RPCs, ceiling=2, floor=1

available.summary: No manifest, resource, probe or PDB touched; readiness/liveness use the gRPC health service, not Hello, so rejections cannot affect rotation.

correct.summary: No contract documents an empty name as valid, no deployed caller sends one (frontend's Home handler is Unimplemented and makes no call to hello; dev traffic generator confirmed non-blank), and .paved-agent/discover.yaml is not platform-owned so check-stamp is unaffected; the description omits a second, minor behavior change (internal padding is now also trimmed from the success path).

observable.summary: The rejection is countable (vikrant_rpcs_handled_total{code="InvalidArgument"}, discover.yaml measure.errors) but no alert rule or dashboard watches it (stack.metrics: 'no alerting rules'; measured ALERTS empty), and there is no runtime off switch short of an image revert — acceptable only because the worst case is dev-only, single-instance, internal.

progressively_delivered.summary: Canary rollout exists but its AnalysisTemplate server-errors query only counts code=~Unknown|Internal|DataLoss|DeadlineExceeded, excluding InvalidArgument — a surge of rejected requests would promote through 10%→50%→100% undetected; only a human watching vikrant_rpcs_handled_total{code="InvalidArgument"} would catch it, and no alert exists.

proven.summary: e2e's reachability check ('reach') and the node-drain 'no-errors' tally both still pass with InvalidArgument responses (neither matches() nor the probe's failure set treats InvalidArgument as a failure), so after this change hello's in-cluster e2e no longer exercises a single successful Hello call at all — a real regression in test coverage that CI will not catch; unit tests cover the new branches but go test could not be executed in this sandbox (no Go toolchain) to confirm `make test` passes.

reversible.summary: No proto, persisted data, or config schema changes; purely additive behavior change, rollback is a plain image revert with no migration.

secure.summary: No new data, field, log line or permission; error message is a constant and does not echo caller input; authorizedCallers/ingress/egress unchanged.

stable_under_failure.summary: InvalidArgument is excluded from both the mesh's idempotent-route retryOn and the client's absent retry policy, so no amplification is possible.

within_budget.summary: No outbound calls added; the rejected path does less work than before; no load added to any dependency.

findings.claim: frontend, the only authorizedCaller (service.yaml authorizedCallers: smallStepGiantLeap/frontend), has no call site to hello.v1.HelloService/Hello in its code at all — its Home handler returns Unimplemented and never dials hello — so no production code path can send a blank name.

evidence.value: zero hits in any .go file; internal/handlers/frontend_service.go:22-25 Home returns codes.Unimplemented

findings.recommendation: None required; note for future review once frontend implements the call.

findings.claim: The description says 'trim the name' but the diff also changes the success path for any caller that sends padded whitespace: '  Ada ' now yields 'hello Ada' instead of the previous literal 'hello   Ada '.

evidence.value: trim applies before greeting() on the success path too

findings.recommendation: Call out the padding-trim as an explicit, separate behavior change in the description.

findings.claim: The PR edits internal/handlers/ (team-owned per README) and .paved-agent/discover.yaml, neither of which appears in .platform/sha256sums, so CI's check-stamp will not reject this PR.

AnalysisTemplate server-errors' prometheus query filters code=~"Unknown|Internal|DataLoss|DeadlineExceeded", which excludes InvalidArgument, so a surge of rejected Hello calls would pass analysis at every canary step (10%, 50%) and reach 100%.
findings.recommendation: Widen the analysis query to include client-error codes relevant to business logic, or accept that this class of regression needs a human watching the InvalidArgument series during rollout.

findings.claim: e2e's reachability check ('CODE InvalidArgument' matches expectation 'reach' since only PermissionDenied|Unavailable|DeadlineExceeded are excluded) and drain_under_load's no-errors tally (InvalidArgument is absent from the probe's failure=[Unavailable,DeadlineExceeded,Internal,Unknown,Canceled] list) both still PASS, so the in-cluster e2e no longer actually proves a successful Hello call exists after this change.

evidence.value: InvalidArgument excluded from both exclusion lists

findings.recommendation: Add an e2e or unit assertion that an authorized caller sending a non-empty name still gets CODE OK with the expected message, since the probe's emptypb.Empty{} always sends name="".

findings.claim: The rejection is countable via vikrant_rpcs_handled_total{code="InvalidArgument"} but no alert rule exists (stack.metrics.is: 'no alerting rules'; measured ALERTS{alertstate="firing",namespace="hello"} returned no data) and there is no flag to disable the new check without a deploy.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable for a dev-only, single-instance, internal-only change; revisit before this path is ever exposed outside dev or to external callers.

summary: No blocking issue: no deployed caller (frontend has no call site to hello at all) can hit the new InvalidArgument path, retries/mesh don't amplify it, and the e2e/CI gates will pass. Two warnings drive the verdict: the canary's AnalysisTemplate ignores InvalidArgument so a real regression would silently promote to 100%, and the same blind spot means e2e no longer exercises a single successful Hello call, with no alert on the new error class either.
